english: For many years there was a fight between the two houses. Then the two came together. This one said to that one: 'Your brother killed my offspring, and my brother killed your offspring. Take the price, and I too will take the price. Peace will be for us.' Then they drank wine together.

english: The man sat down at the fire and made the oath. 'The sun has seen me, the fire heard me, the water knows me. I did not steal the cart. If I speak a lie, may the fire burn me, may the water swallow me, and may the sun not catch sight of me.'

english: Whoever steals, night hides him; the sun has seen him. Whoever drives off horses, the dog knows him. The wolf comes in the night; the shepherd stays awake. The man who steals eats and is not satisfied.

english: Two brothers were before the king. This one said: 'These cattle are mine.' That one said: 'They are not yours; they are mine.' Then he said: 'Cattle know their own master. english: A brother is a brother's arm. Whoever kills his brother cuts off his own arm. A man has two arms, a house has two brothers. A lone sheep is the wolf's meat.

english: A woman went to the king and said: 'My horse is gone.' Then he said to the shepherd: 'Track it.' Then the shepherd tracked it along the path and found it in the enclosure of a man. Then he said: 'How is the horse in your enclosure?' 'I found it on the path.' 'Did you speak to the woman?' 'I did not speak to her.' 'Give it to the woman again. Whoever finds and does not speak, he steals.'

english: Master, listen to my pledge! I will guard your sheep for a year. I will lead them to the water and drive them home at night, and at night I will stay awake, and I will work for you. If a wolf seizes a sheep, I will give you a sheep. If I lie to you, may the gods strike me down. Give me my wage.

english: Two women went to the king and said: 'The sheep is mine.' Then he said: 'Shepherd, split the sheep in two!' Then this one said: 'Split it.' That one cried out: 'Do not split it! Let it be this one's, and let it live.' Then he said: 'You are its mistress. Take it.'

english: The two fathers sat down together and drank wine. This one gave that one a plough; that one gave this one a boat. Then this one said: 'Let there be a bond between the two houses. May our sons be friends. Let no one break the pledge.'

english: 'Will you make the oath?' 'I will make it.' 'Whom do you fear?' 'I fear Father Sky. He has seen what is hidden. If I lie to him, may he strike me down, and may my offspring not grow.'

english: The father-in-law and the son-in-law were before the king. The father-in-law said: 'He did not bring me the bride price.' 'Son-in-law, did you give the bride price?' 'I gave ten cattle.' 'Who saw it?' 'I saw it.' 'Son-in-law, you have spoken the truth. Father-in-law, you spoke a lie. Honor your son-in-law.'

english: A man made an oath and broke it. The gods saw him. Then his barley vanished, his house fell and his offspring was gone. Then death seized him, and no one honored him. Fire guards the oath. A man dies; an oath does not die.

english: Father Sky, you who protect the guest, guard him on the path. Mother Earth, carry him. May his path be straight, and may the star show him the path, and may the sun warm him. May the wolf not seize him. May he come to his own house, and may his mother see him.

english: It was getting dark, and a guest arrived at the king's house. Then the king stood up, took hold of his arm and led him inside and seated him on a seat. Then the queen carried meat and honey to him. Then he ate and was sated. The king said: 'Lie down. When the dawn has shone, tell me your name.'

english: The two sons rose against one another. Then the mother stood up between them and spoke: 'You are born of me. I nourished you. Sons, hit me! Let no one kill his own brother.' Then the two heard her and sat down on the earth. Peace came to them.

english: Last year the master gave the guest a yoke. Yesterday the guest came again to the master's house, carrying a gift. Then he looked at it, became joyful, and spoke: 'A gift went out from my house, and a gift has come again to my house. Sit down, and eat together.' Then the two ate.

pie: h₃réǵ ḱā́m bʰoydʰéh₂m dʰéh₁m̥. pró h₁éyoh₂. mē bʰugyéh₁m̥. méroh₂ wénoh₂-wē ń̥dʰgʷʰitom ḱléwos. dyéw me dedórḱth₂e. h₁yód bʰéwgoh₂ dʰéǵʰōm me gʷr̥h₃óyh₁t. h₁nómn̥ moy ḱlutóm bʰúHeti.
english: King, I have made this pledge: I will go forward. May I not flee. I shall die, or I shall win imperishable fame. Sky, you have seen me. If I flee, may the earth swallow me. My name will become famous.

english: This one broke that one's boat. Then the king said: 'If anyone takes the boat of his own brother and the boat sinks, let him give him a boat. If the brother gave it and it sinks, let him not give anything. The boat is the brother's.'

english: The guest ate and drank. Then he said: 'Guest, now you are satisfied. Who are you? Where are you going? Is your mother alive?' 'I am the son of a shepherd. I am going to my brother's house. My mother is alive; my father is not.' 'Lie down in my dwelling, and the night will bring you rest.' Then he lay down.

english: Father Sky, hear me! Mother Earth, listen! I did not steal my kinsman's horse. If I speak a lie, may you strike me down, Sky, and may the earth not nourish me. If I speak the truth, may I live and see the dawn, and may my house stand.

english: The guest stood up, and the master went with him and spoke: 'This rock stands in my field; that path is yours. Go in peace. Remember this house. When you come again to my house, I will honor you.'

english: A man went to the king and spoke: 'My brother's cattle ate my barley. What shall he give me?' Then he said: 'Let him give you barley, and let him build a hedge. A hedge guards peace.' Then he built the hedge.

english: Kinsmen, listen! The fight devoured men. Let the earth cover the slain, and let peace be a shelter for you. Let the fight lie down. Lift the plough and plough the field. May the two households live.

english: The priest said to the king: "Pray to the god Werunos."

english: A gift seeks a gift. Whoever gives receives; whoever does not give does not receive. A gift does not vanish. A gift from a good heart is dear. The giver of good things is dear.
